business_scope.primary_industry_name: Stock Photography Marketplace and Generative Visual Assets

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national system; French commercial law codified in the Code de commerce and applicable EU regulations)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-United States Double Taxation Convention (1994, as amended by the 2006 and 2009 Protocols)
France-Germany Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement (1959, as amended), supplemented by the EU Arbitration Convention 90/436/EEC
France-China Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement (signed 2 November 2013; in force from 14 December 2015)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (Articles 49 and 54 TFEU on right of establishment; Article 56 TFEU on free provision of services)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (French Monetary and Financial Code), Articles L.561-1 through L.561-57 (AML/CFT customer due diligence, UBO identification, PEP rules) and Articles L.562-1 through L.562-13 (asset freezing); Code de commerce, Article R.123-163 et seq. (Register of Beneficial Owners maintained at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS); EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843, transposed by French ordinances and decrees; the UBO declaration filing obligation is governed by CMF Article L.561-46 and related implementing decrees.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (public access restricted following CJEU jurisprudence on beneficial-ownership registers; authorized government bodies and obliged entities with legitimate AML/CFT interest retain access)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport or national identity document of each individual shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or civil registry/notary in the shareholder's country of origin or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (date-stamped by the competent apostille authority of the country of issue) OR Consular Legalization by the French Embassy/Consulate for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO/shareholder (utility bill, bank statement, or administrative certificate, dated less than three months prior)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, credit institution, or competent local authority in the shareholder's place of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; final acceptance condition: certified French translation by an accredited court-appointed translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, registry extract, or certificate of good standing for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar or commercial registry ministry of the corporate shareholder's home state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, followed by sworn French translation for filing with the RCS and the UBO declaration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residence certificate of each shareholder when treaty benefits or withholding-rate privileges are claimed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax authority of the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the receiving French bank or registry so requires; otherwise original consular-lawful copy retained in the AML due-diligence file

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all identified shareholders, UBOs, and the designated gérant against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and the French national asset-freeze list maintained under Code monétaire et financier Article L.562-3; PEP identification and enhanced due diligence are mandatory under CMF Articles L.561-10 and R.561-17 et seq.; OFAC SDN screening is adopted as institutional best practice where USD settlement or US nexus exists; given the Low_Risk_Standard AML tier of the stock-media commercial model, standard customer due diligence with UBO identification and risk-based EDD is sufficient, with ongoing transaction monitoring delegated to the acquiring bank and the Stripe/PayPal payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by the INPI; name availability cross-verified against the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE), the Infogreffe database, and the INPI trademark register
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The dénomination sociale may contain words of foreign origin, but the name must be rendered in Latin characters for indexing in the RNE and RCS; non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, Arabic, CJK) require a transliterated Latin version used in the statutes and all registry filings; the suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or 'SARL' and the share capital must be stated in all corporate documentation and commercial communication; the name must not create confusion or similarity with prior registered company names or protected trademarks, and all French-language registry submissions control over translations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque (requires ACPR or ECB credit-institution authorization)
Assurance (requires ACPR authorization under the French Insurance Code)
Crédit (reserved term under French banking legislation)
Fiduciaire (restricted under Code monétaire et financier provisions)
Mutuelle (reserved for mutual insurance entities regulated by special statutes)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected by the registry controller or the greffe, the incorporator must first amend the constitution file and resubmit the corrected name through the Guichet Unique within 15 days of the notification; if objection persists, the applicant may file a written appeal within two months of rejection before the President of the competent Tribunal de Commerce (or Tribunal Judiciaire in non-commercial matters) by way of a summary application, seeking annulment of the registrar's decision; where the conflict arises from a third-party trademark, the applicant may file an opposition action with the INPI, obtain a coexistence consent or settlement assignment, or otherwise abandon the conflicting name; all appeal materials must be in French and supported by certified translations where applicable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable: a French SARL may maintain its registered office at an approved commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) under Articles L.123-10 et seq. and R.123-166 of the French Commercial Code, provided a one-year renewable domiciliation contract is in force, official correspondence is handled, and the registered address permits physical receipt of administrative and judicial documents; for an ISIC 7420 stock-photo and generative visual-assets platform with no statutory license requirement, a domiciliation agreement is commercially sufficient, but the SARL must retain accounting books, corporate minutes, and operational records accessible at the declared address and must be able to demonstrate real management substance upon request of the tax administration or URSSAF.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: quantified annual probability of approximately 5% for a non-licensed digital-service SARL; unannounced on-site inspections occur mainly in the context of criminal, fiscal, or anti-fraud warrants, or as targeted greffe controls on domiciliation compliance within the first 24 months; the domiciliation provider should be contractually required to cooperate with inspections and immediately notify the gérant.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS incorporation registration filing fee (immatriculation au registre du commerce et des sociétés)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the Guichet Unique (INPI/formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by Ministry of Justice arrêté for RCS filings; fixed fee expressed in EUR

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the statutory incorporation notice (avis de constitution) in an approved legal-announcements journal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized for the jurisdiction of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated market rate per insertion; by-line tariff published by the JAL

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the French articles of association (statuts), including the UBO declaration template and AML/CFT compliance file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee market benchmark for a standard SARL with non-resident shareholders and low-risk digital activity (EUR 2,500-3,500 plus VAT)
Annual market benchmark of EUR 80-200 per month depending on Paris/region and supplementary services; one-year binding contract

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified sworn translation of foreign shareholder/UBO identity and corporate documents into French
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-appointed certified translator (traducteur inscrit près une cour d'appel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-page market tariff of EUR 25-40 per page; estimated for a 20-30 page dossier

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of the UBO identity and address bundle for non-French shareholders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the document's country of origin and/or French Embassy/Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official per-document fees of the issuing state plus French consular legalization fee where applicable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary name-clearance search across RNE, Infogreffe, and INPI trademark database, plus issuance of the registration file's extracts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI data platform and Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS extract)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fees; online search free of charge, certified paper extract subject to official greffe fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 et seq., L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL), and R.123-30 et seq. (RCS registration), as amended by Law No. 2021-1300 (DDADUE), implemented through the Guichet Unique operated by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office, via the INPI-operated Guichet Unique Electronique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de constitution de société au RCS (Cerfa N/S0 form) together with the notarized or private Articles of Association (statuts), filed electronically on the Guichet Unique
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital is required; the share capital may be set at EUR 1 or any higher amount, but each share must be fully subscribed. At least 20% of the nominal value of each share must be paid up at subscription and deposited in a blocked escrow bank account until the RCS registration is completed. The unpaid balance may be called by the manager within five years.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Unanimous Written Resolution of the Sole Shareholder / General Meeting of the SARL, dated [date]. Resolved: (a) that the share capital of EUR 1,000 be subscribed in full by the partners and that at least 20% be paid up to the specified capital escrow account prior to filing; (b) that the registered office be established at [address] in [city], France; (c) that [name] be appointed as Gérant (general manager) with authority to act on behalf of the company, sign all incorporation filings, and complete the RCS registration; (d) that any necessary powers of attorney, legal advertisements, and certificates of incorporation be executed accordingly. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Document Preparation and Capital Blocking
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; not notarization mandatory unless a contribution in kind or real property is made
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association (statuts) in French, allocating share quotas to the partners and appointing the first gérant. Open a blocked capital deposit account at a French bank, deposit at least 20% of the subscribed capital, and obtain the capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds). Obtain proof of the registered office, such as a signed lease or a letter from the owner granting domiciliation.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (statuts)
Valid identity documents of all partners and the proposed gérant
Déclaration de non-condamnation and CV of the gérant
Bank certificate of capital deposit
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to block the funds, the deposit may be made through a notaire's escrow account; otherwise, replace the bank and initiate a new blocked-account attestation. Any query regarding KYC documentation must be cured within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Legal Announcement of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved legal gazette (Journal d'annonces légales) in the département of the registered office, or an approved online platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an incorporation notice (avis de constitution) to the legal gazette including the proposed company name, SARL form, share capital, registered office, corporate object, gérant details, and RCS registry where the company will be registered. After verification, obtain the attestation de publication to be attached to the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Text of the legal notice
Draft Articles of Association summary
Identity details of the gérant
Payment receipt for publication fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is refused or delayed, correct the factual inconsistencies, verify the exact département of the registered office, and resubmit the notice to the same or another approved gazette.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Application on the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique Electronique and the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, select the SARL creation workflow, and complete the standard Cerfa N/S0 declaration. Upload certified copies of the signed Articles of Association, the capital deposit certificate, the legal announcement attestation, proof of registered office, identity documents, and the Declaration of Beneficial Owner (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs). Pay the required registration fee electronically and submit the dossier for statutory review.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of final Articles of Association
Attestation de dépôt de fonds for the paid-up capital
Attestation de publication de l'avis de constitution
Proof of registered office (lease or domiciliation letter)
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs (DBE)
Sworn statement of the gérant on absence of conviction
Copy of passport or national ID of the gérant and partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe or INPI issues an incompleteness notice, submit the missing documents through the Guichet Unique within 15 calendar days. If the application is rejected, correct the substantive mistake and file a new application; no re-filing fee applies if the original dossier is rectified within the prescribed period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the K-Bis Extract and SIREN/SIRET Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, in coordination with INSEE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation by the Greffe, the company is registered on the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, assigned a SIREN number and SIRET codes, and issued the official Extrait K-bis. Download or request the certified K-bis and verify the legal identity, corporate form, capital, registered office, and gérant information.
required_dossiers: Validated RCS filing receipt from the Guichet Unique
Proof of payment of registration fees
Final Articles of Association as accepted by the Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis is not generated because of incomplete INSEE data, ask the Greffe to re-issue the extract after confirming the SIRET code synchronization. If there is a delay, file a written expedited request with the competent Greffe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Completion and Post-Registration Declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gérant and shareholders; French tax authorities (DGFiP); social security administration (URSSAF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first meeting of the shareholders or obtain the written resolution approving the Articles of Association, the registration steps, and the opening of the corporate bank account. Compile the minutes, maintain the company's corporate register, affix the corporate seal if required, and complete any separate registrations for VAT, payroll, or commercial insurance. If the company will have employees, file the employer declaration with URSSAF.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first general meeting or written resolution
K-bis extract
Corporate bank account opening certificate
VAT registration application if not automatically registered
Employer declaration to URSSAF if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If social or tax administrations flag missing declarations, cure by filing the relevant form on the portal of the competent agency and present the corrected declaration to the Greffe for any corporate record update.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial establishment is required for a commercial stock-photo and generative visual assets platform operating online
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no statutory industrial operating or manufacturing permit is required under the ICPE (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement) nomenclature for this tertiary service activity

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable - no fixed installation subject to environmental impact assessment; if a physical server or manufacturing site is later established, the relevant authority is DREAL in coordination with the Préfecture
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - online stock-media service activity outside the categories requiring a full environmental impact assessment or environmental registration
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - the activity generates no process wastewater, volatile organic compound emissions, or regulated physical waste streams; operations rely on cloud infrastructure and standard commercial IT equipment

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil-defense or fire-safety certification is required for a purely digital platform; if a physical office is opened, it must comply with the Code du travail safety rules, building fire-safety standards, and applicable workplace accessibility requirements, and if the premises are classified as ERP, the Programme de Sécurité and fire inspection must be obtained.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal https://www.impots.gouv.fr; company and VAT identification formalities are processed through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises at https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned French SARL, the statutory registration path requires submission of the incorporation dossier (statuts, nomination of manager, proof of registered office, declaration of beneficial ownership) to the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (CFE). The CFE transmits the file to the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE), the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), and the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE). Upon completion, the SARL obtains its SIREN/SIRET numbers. For VAT purposes, the DGFiP verifies the economic activity and, where the entity is not covered by the small-business exemption, allocates an individual VAT identification number (numéro d'identification individuel) and, for intra-EU transactions, the FR VAT number reported to the VIES system. Non-established foreign entities carrying out taxable supplies in France may apply directly to the DGFiP for a VAT registration using form SI-355/FR.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SARL is by default subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at entity level. Under Article 239 bis AA of the French General Tax Code (CGI), a small SARL meeting statutory criteria (fewer than ten employees, turnover below the thresholds set by decree, and ownership by natural persons) may elect, for a maximum of five fiscal years, to be taxed as a partnership (société de personnes) with profits passed through to shareholders (impôt sur le revenu, IR). The option must be notified to the tax authorities. Additionally, certain SARL de famille may be taxed as IR entities. Hybrid mismatch consequences are addressed through mandatory disclosure and neutralisation rules under EU ATAD implementation, Article 212 bis CGI, and B2B notification obligations under DAC6; France does not apply a US-style check-the-box regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: French VAT registration is generally mandatory for any taxable person established in France making taxable supplies, without an annual turnover threshold; however, the statutory small-business exemption (franchise en base de TVA) under CGI Article 293 B applies to resident taxable persons whose annual turnover (exclusive of VAT) does not exceed EUR 91,900 for principal supplies of goods and EUR 36,800 for principal supplies of services. For intra-EU remote supplies of digital services and distance sales of goods to non-taxable persons, the pan-EU registration threshold is EUR 10,000 of aggregate cross-border turnover, above which the supplier must register for VAT in each relevant Member State or use the One-Stop Shop (OSS) simplified regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has implemented a mandatory electronic invoicing and e-reporting regime, phasing in from 1 September 2026 for large and mid-market entities and from 1 September 2027 for SMEs and micro-enterprises. All B2B invoices must be issued as structured electronic invoices (Factur-X, UBL, or CII) through an accredited Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) or the public Portal Public de Facturation (PPF), which transmits invoice data in near-real-time to the DGFiP. E-reporting of B2C transaction data is also mandatory. France does not operate a fiscal pre-clearance stamping model; instead, it requires API-based structured data transmission ensuring end-to-end integrity and auditability. Non-resident suppliers subject to French VAT must either register in France or, for intra-EU B2C digital services, use the OSS portal, with equivalent e-reporting obligations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the supply of goods physically exported from France to destinations outside the European Union, provided that the exporter or the acquirer dispatches or transports the goods outside the EU within the statutory time frame and retains evidence of export (CGI Article 262 and Annex I Article 74 A). Services physically performed in France but directly related to exported goods (e.g., handling, transport, inspection) may also be zero-rated under French law. For B2B digital services such as stock photography licensing supplied to a customer established outside the EU, the place of supply is the customer's jurisdiction and the supply is outside the scope of French VAT; the French supplier may deduct attributable input VAT, subject to standard substantiation rules. For B2C digital services supplied to non-EU consumers, the supply is also outside the scope of French VAT. To claim zero-rating or out-of-scope treatment, the taxpayer must hold sufficient documentary evidence identifying the destination of the goods or the establishment of the customer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation via DELTA) with MRN (Movement Reference Number)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill / CMR / consignment note) evidencing physical dispatch from the EU
Commercial invoice and contract evidencing the terms of sale and the foreign customer's identity
Bank transfer or inward remittance certificate evidencing the receipt payment in foreign currency or euro from the non-resident customer
Supporting evidence of customer establishment for out-of-scope services (e.g., VAT registration certificate, extract of foreign commercial register)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French tax authorities aggressively audit export zero-rating claims and out-of-scope service treatments. If the required export evidence is absent, defective, or fraudulent, VAT becomes immediately collectible together with interest (intérêts de retard) at the statutory monthly rate. Penalties under CGI Article 1788 and Article 1728 include a 10% to 40% increase for omissions or inaccuracies; an 80% penalty applies for bad faith (manvais foi) or obstruction; a 100% penalty applies for abusive arrangements under CGI Article 1729 and Article 1731. Criminal liability may arise under Articles 1741, 1742, and 1743 of the French General Tax Code for fraudulent tax evasion, with imprisonment up to five years and fines up to EUR 75,000 per individual and EUR 375,000 for legal entities. Retrospective clawbacks may extend to up to five fiscal years (or ten years in the event of abuse of law), with the burden of proof shifted where the taxpayer fails to maintain credible documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF), under the Eurosystem framework, in coordination with the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) for prudential and conduct supervision, and the Direction Générale du Trésor for foreign-exchange and investment regulatory policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a Member State of the Economic and Monetary Union; the euro is fully convertible for both current-account operations (royalties, trade in services, freelancer remuneration) and capital-account operations (share capital injections, dividend distributions, repayment of shareholder loans). No prior exchange authorization is needed for payment in or out of the country, including for non-resident shareholders. The only practical limitations are EU/OFAC sanctions compliance and a mandatory monthly Balance-of-Payments (BoP) reporting obligation to the Banque de France for any individual cross-border monetary transfer equal to or exceeding EUR 12,500, usually filed by the banking intermediary. Profit remittances to an EU shareholder are unrestricted; remittances to a non-EU shareholder are free but must pass standard anti-money-laundering checks and will be automatically exchanged with the shareholder's tax authority under Common Reporting Standard (CRS) obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: French law does not impose any statutory surrender or mandatory foreign-exchange conversion ratio for export proceeds, regardless of currency. The French Monetary and Financial Code (Code Monétaire et Financier, Art. L.112-4, R.112-1) permits free retention of foreign currency in bank accounts with a French credit institution or abroad, provided the underlying commercial operation is documented and the associated cross-border flow above EUR 12,500 is reported to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics. The SARL may invoice and receive settlement in EUR for all exports, or in any foreign currency agreed by the parties. Commercial prudence suggests converting or hedging non-EUR receipts to eliminate currency mismatch, but no regulatory timeline exists for repatriation once the receivable is recorded.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) during formation, followed by an Operational Multi-Currency Account (EUR/USD/GBP)
Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) and Operational Account with trade finance and FX hedging desk
Operational Account in EUR and foreign currencies; capital escrow service available

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — French licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto, Shine, or Pennylane are feasible as a supplementary operating account for SEPA collections and low-value royalty payouts, but they cannot execute documentary trade instruments, provide committed FX facilities, or act as a capital-formation deposit bank under CMF Art. L525-1. For the target ISIC 7420 stock-photo AI business with expected cross-border MDR (merchant discounts) and international payout streams, an EMI is acceptable for aggregated receivables under EUR 20,000/month, but a robust treasury requires a Tier-1 bank for FIC-regulated BoP reporting, correspondent banking, and bare-metal FX settlement. EMI onboarding is legally valid via ACPR-approved video-identification; no physical presence is required.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, a Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) must undergo a physical onboarding interview at a French bank branch for the gérant (managing director) and, if non-resident, for any individual holding 25% or more of share capital. Full remote opening is possible only if the bank has implemented an ACPR-approved video-identification mechanism (Décret n° 2018-1226) and the SARL's corporate documents are digitally notarized or apostilled. For foreign non-resident managing directors, banks usually require an original apostilled power of attorney appointing a French resident as corporate representative, accompanied by the physical passport and proof of residence; in exceptional cases, a face-to-face interview at a French consulate can substitute. The use of an unregulated foreign lawyer as intermediary is generally insufficient for the first KYC interview unless the law firm is mandated under a notarized French proxy and the bank accepts a 'know your customer' certificate from a sister EU bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SARL with one or more non-resident shareholders, no local audited financial history, and a fully digital revenue model originating outside the EU — a standard financial-crime red flag for foreign shell risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully certified dossier comprising: (i) Kbis extract and notarized statutory bylaws (statuts); (ii) final beneficial-ownership register extract from the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés; (iii) certified passports and utility bills for all UBOs; (iv) tax residency certificates of each shareholder; (v) bank reference letter from the shareholder's current bank; (vi) source-of-funds documentation (tax returns, salary slips, business asset sales, bank account statements covering minimum 12 months); (vii) sworn declaration of economic purpose and an in-confidence business plan for the stock-photo AI venture; (viii) French counsel legal opinion that the structure does not constitute a conduit for tax or money-laundering risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency global collection of royalty and advertising payments from multiple Marketplace platforms, aggregators, and foreign licensees — suspicious 'pass-through' liquidity covering potential layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the bank with: (i) signed marketplace distribution agreements (Stripe, PayPal, Adobe Stock, Getty contributory, etc.); (ii) a detailed ledger traceability report showing each upstream invoice and downstream payout; (iii) certified financial statements or quarterly management accounts; (iv) an up-to-date map of professional counterparties with country list and legal identifiers; (v) evidence of operational substance, such as a French office lease, third-party hosting contracts, domain ownership, and a dedicated accountant; (vi) an internal AML self-assessment checklist aligned with the ACPR AML/CFT guideline on digital asset providers; (vii) letters from major marketplaces confirming their own KYC/AML adherence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border disbursements to non-EU photographers and content producers using international wire transfers or EMI settlement — appears as an inward-outward payment mismatch without clear commercial justification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The SARL must submit: (i) a complete list of beneficiary content providers, their bank data, and tax identification numbers; (ii) copies of the licensing/commission contracts and the platform copyright notice; (iii) payout reconciliation reports showing that each transfer is a standard royalty; (iv) documentary evidence that no beneficiary is screened by EU/OFAC sanctions list; (v) the ACPR-compliant AML framework for designated non-financial business obligations; (vi) the last financial year's audited statement (if any) or a certified management accountant report; (vii) a legal memorandum that the entity is a licensing intermediary, not a mere payment pass-through, and therefore the SARL is not an 'acknowledged agent' under CMF Art. L. 561-2-1.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the French SARL, whether initial or subsequent, must be credited to a French bank account held in the corporate name. Transfer protocols: send SWIFT MT103 where the remittance information field clearly states 'Apport en capital / Subscription to shares' and includes the corporate corporate identifier (SIREN/LEI) of the SARL. For any inflow exceeding EUR 12,500 in one calendar month, the receiving bank will execute the balance-of-payments declaration (Balances des Paiements) to the Banque de France; no separate client filing is required, but the company must retain a copy of the transaction letter for tax and legal audit. If the shareholder is outside the EU, the capital injection may trigger a declaration of direct investment to the Ministère de l'Économie (form CERFA n° 10874*) only if the activity falls under a sensitive sector (which ISIC 7420 does not) and the investor acquires more than 25% of the company's voting rights. No prior special authorization applies to a stock-photo licensing business; however, the bank will request evidence that the injection derives from legal funds, and for a contribution in kind (such as a software licence or photolibrary valuation), a statutory auditor's report (commissaire aux apports) is mandatory.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements—including royalty payments, stock-photo licence fees, artificial-intelligence model dataset purchase agreements, and any all-in price from foreign content creators—the preferred clearing rails are: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (MT103 or ISO 20022 pain.001) for EEA beneficiaries in EUR; (ii) ordinary SWIFT MT103 with correspondent bank for non-EEA beneficiaries; (iii) local ACH/FPS clearing for USD/GBP if the collection account holds multi-currency balances to minimize bank charges; and (iv) international wire using a designated beneficiary celling for payouts above USD 100,000. Commercial Letters of Credit are not required for software/royalty flows and are not business-as-usual for a stock-photo marketplace; standby letters of credit or documentary collections (URC 522) appear only when the SARL acquires an entire photographic asset library or content portfolio from a foreign legal owner. Every outbound disbursement over EUR 10,000 is automatically screened by the bank for terrorism and sanctions; the airway bill, copyright transfer memorandum, or platform payout report must be attached to the instruction when a non-standard remittance (e.g., buy-out of catalogues) is requested. For regular distributions of profits to shareholders, a corporate resolution of the gérant and a distribution attestation from the professional accountant are required; the bank may block the payment if the SARL is in a 'quasi-capital' deficit or if the funds have not, as of the distribution date, cleared from the concerned transaction account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot transactions (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/JPY) with value date T+2 at regulated financial counterparty under French banking law
Outright FX forward contracts up to 24 months, provided the counterparty is a licensed French or EU credit institution and the hedge is documented as commercial cover for expected royalty cash flows
FX swaps (two-date, both legs on fixed amounts) used for short-term treasury liquidity management
Cross-currency swaps (interest-rate and principal exchange) for medium-term refinancing of foreign-currency receivables, executed under ISDA 2002 with a French bank

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies of jurisdictions with strict convertibility controls (e.g., certain Central American, East Asian, or West African floating currencies), where the nominal is settled in EUR, authorised under the prevailing French regulatory regime if the underlying is a bona-fide commercial trade or a foreign-currency receivable
Currency options (EUR call / foreign currency put, and vice versa) on standard major pairs, embedded in a vanilla premium with ACPR/MIFID suitability test

FX futures through regulated French markets (Euronext Paris and NYSE Liffe) when exchange-traded derivative positions are OFC-cleared, and only if the treasury counterparty qualifies under Article 324-2 of the AMF General Regulation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of accounts by shareholders (Assemblée Générale Ordinaire) and recording of minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General shareholders' meeting (internal corporate act; minutes retained in the statutory minute book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June; extension obtainable from the Commercial Court upon reasoned request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 9,000 on each manager for failure to convene the shareholders' meeting within 6 months of year-end (Art. L.241-5 Code de commerce); nullity exposure for shareholder decisions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements deposit (Dépôt des comptes annuels) to the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI via the RCS electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month (electronic deposit) or 2 months (paper deposit) after the shareholders' approval meeting; maximum fallback date approximately 31 July for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry formal notice (mise en demeure); court injunction with daily astreinte; criminal fine of EUR 9,000 on managers; administrative strike-off from the RCS after two consecutive years of non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale — déclaration 2065-SD with annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques) via the EFI professional e-filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the 2nd working day following 1 May (paper 3 May) and by 18 May for mandatory EFI e-filers where the fiscal year coincides with the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-filing surcharge (reported up to 30 days after deadline); 40% bad-faith penalty; 80% fraudulent-conduct penalty; 0.20% monthly late-payment interest; EUR 150 fine per missing or incomplete schedule; ex-officio assessment after 60 days of silence

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business tax — Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP / local municipal tax collection office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Tax roll issued in the fourth quarter; payment due by 15 December of the billing year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment penalty plus 0.20% per month late-payment interest; enforced Treasury recovery with bank seizure risk; CFE remains due even for fully digital activity if premises or minimum tax basis exist

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register maintenance (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) and declaration updates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI — registry file (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No standalone annual UBO form; any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days; the register is audited each year by the registry during the annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 15,000 for natural persons and EUR 75,000 for legal persons for non-declaration; same amounts for knowingly false declarations; potential corporate lock prohibited for share transactions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) for an SARL when at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded: (i) balance-sheet total above EUR 4,000,000; (ii) turnover (HT) above EUR 8,000,000; (iii) average 50+ employees during the year. Shareholders holding above 15% of capital may also request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP per the Plan Comptable Général as codified by the Autorité des Normes Comptables (ANC regulation 2018-06); IFRS is not mandatory for a standalone unlisted SARL; micro-entity and simplified presentation rules apply where eligibility thresholds are met.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation form; however, every share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be declared to the commercial registry within 30 days, and the internal UBO register must be continuously updated. The greffe cross-checks UBO data during the annual accounts deposit.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share transfers and security interests (registre des mouvements de parts sociales)
Register of shareholders' decisions and minutes (registre des délibérations et procès-verbaux)
Register of managers' decisions (registre des décisions des gérants)
Register of beneficial owners (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $250 - $800 per annum (dependent on the commercial domiciliation provider and Paris vs. regional rate)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $5,000 - $18,000 per annum for a compulsory audit engagement; generally not applicable to a micro SARL that remains below the legal auditor thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on taxable profits up to €42,500 for qualifying SMEs (turnover below €10 million and at least 75% held by individuals). No general statutory tax holiday. R&D tax credit (Crédit Impôt Recherche, CIR) available for eligible AI software and asset-generation R&D costs, and innovation tax credit (CII) for certain prototype and industrial property expenses. Depreciation of software and image databases is deductible.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: French corporate income tax return: Form 2065-SD (liassez fiscale 2065) accompanied by the full financial statements (bilan, compte de résultat, annexes) submitted electronically via impots.gouv.fr through the EDI-TDFC or EFI filing portals.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For entities with a fiscal year ending 31 December, the filing deadline is the second business day following 1 May of the subsequent year. For a fiscal year ending on a date other than 31 December, the deadline is the second business day following 1 May after the last day of the fiscal year. Advance instalments (acomptes) are paid quarterly during the year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies the SARL: corporate name, SIREN, SIRET, registered office address, tax identification number, legal form and principal activity code (NAF/APE code 7420Z).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL must identify its French permanent establishment (PE) number and confirm that a PE exists in France; state whether the PE is a branch or constitutes a place of effective management in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2065-SD, Box B (Bilan actif) and Box C (Bilan passif)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet assets and liabilities. For an AI stock photo platform, asset lines include intangible assets (software, image databases, generative model licences), trade receivables, and cash.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must allocate to the French PE all assets attributable to French-source revenue-generating activities, including servers, contracts, and intellectual property owned by the PE. Cross-border intercompany receivables must be reported at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit and loss statement: turnover includes licensing fees, royalties, subscription revenue and commissions from the stock photo platform, minus cost of sales, operating expenses, depreciation, and financial charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source revenue attributable to the PE under the DTA and French domestic sourcing rules. Deduct only costs actually borne by the PE and supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting profit to taxable income: add back non-deductible expenses (e.g. excessive management fees, fines, non-deductible taxes), apply tax loss carryforward, and account for tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident, ensure that all French-source profits are brought into the taxable base and that losses of foreign head office are not deducted against French PE profit unless expressly allowed under the DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares eligible tax credits, especially the CIR for AI research expenditure (salaries, external R&D, depreciation of research equipment) and the CII for innovative prototypes, if qualifying.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax credits are generally available only for R&D physically carried out in France by the PE. Document the location and substance of AI development activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirms whether the entity applies the standard 25% rate or the reduced 15% rate on the first €42,500 of profit, and confirms the international tax treatment including DTA elections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PE may apply the reduced rate if all eligibility conditions are met. Attach a DTA relief form if claiming treaty benefits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: States how the accounting profit is appropriated: to legal reserve (5% of profit up to 10% of share capital), distribution as dividends, or carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If profits are distributed to a non-resident shareholder, this box triggers the dividend withholding tax obligations and the reporting of the distribution on Form 2561 or equivalent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic penalty of 5% of the tax due, increased to 10% where the return is not filed within 30 days after formal notice. Monthly surcharge of 0.5% of the tax due (max 10% overall). Late payment: interest of 0.2% per month. Failure to report income: 40% penalty for bad faith and 80% for fraudulent behaviour. Director liability for unpaid corporate tax if the managing director fails to file or knowingly files incomplete returns.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends distributed to non-resident corporate shareholders; 30% (12.8% income tax + 17.2% social levies) on dividends paid to non-resident individuals, unless a lower treaty rate applies. Domestic French shareholders may benefit from the participation exemption (parent-subsidiary regime) reducing effective withholding to 0% for EU parents under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced withholding rate under a DTA, the non-resident shareholder must submit to the French paying agent or DGFiP: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority; (ii) a completed Form 5000 (for individuals) or Form 5001 (for entities) claiming treaty benefits; (iii) a declaration of beneficial ownership. For EU parents, a holding-period declaration (minimum 2 years or 24 months) and REIN or Cerfa forms are required. Refund procedures for excess withholding are made by filing a claim within the statutory limitation period (generally until 31 December of the second year following the payment date).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Outbound royalties: statutory withholding tax at 33.33% (including social levies), reduced to 0% or 5% under many DTAs (e.g. France-UK 0%, France-US 5%, France-Netherlands 0%, France-Germany 0% when beneficial owner is a company). Outbound interest: statutory withholding 33.33% unless an exemption for EU companies applies (Parent-Subsidiary Directive or Interest-Royalties Directive); treaty rates commonly 0% or 10%. For stock photo AI licensing, payments for copyrighted image use are considered royalties and may be subject to French withholding when paid by a French entity to a foreign beneficiary; inbound license income received by the French SARL from abroad is not subject to French withholding and foreign taxes are creditable under DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full transfer pricing documentation (Master File and Local File) is mandatory where the group's consolidated turnover exceeds €400 million and the French entity's intra-group transactions exceed €400 million per year. Simplified documentation (a one-page summary) is required for small and medium enterprises (PME) with cross-border intra-group flows exceeding €50,000 per year. Under French law, documentation rules apply to entities subject to corporate income tax with related-party transactions, regardless of turnover, if the tax administration requests it.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies the EU Economic Substance Requirements indirectly through the EU blacklist and DAC6 mandatory disclosure rules. A French SARL must demonstrate real economic substance in France: actual offices, personnel, management decisions, and local operational activity. Artificial arrangements with no substance that shift profits to zero-tax jurisdictions are subject to the General Anti-Abuse Rule (Article L.64 of the French Tax Procedure Code), the altered substance doctrine under Article 155-A, and the Principal Purpose Test in DTAs. The stock photo AI platform must maintain records of hosting, servers, staff, and customer contracts in France to avoid being re-characterised as a shell or conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful filing of false tax returns or deliberate omission of substantial revenue from AI stock photo licensing, under-reporting turnover, or concealing foreign bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (under Article 1741 of the French General Tax Code). Administrative penalty: 40% bad-faith penalty, 80% fraudulent concealment penalty, plus late payment interest at 0.2% per month. Publication of the sanction may be ordered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may be jointly and severally liable for the tax debts and penalties if they personally participated in the evasion; imprisonment and travel bans apply. Civil restitution of evaded taxes with interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Artificial Arrangements (Abus de droit / Société écran)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a French SARL as a shell to pass AI stock photo licensing income to a zero-tax foreign affiliate without real economic substance, or creating a tax-advantageous arrangement lacking a bona fide commercial purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment under the abuse of law procedure (Article L.64) with a penalty of 80% if abusive, or 40% for lack of economic substance. The tax administration may disregard the arrangement and tax the true beneficiary. Extended statute of limitations (10 years instead of 6).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for the recomputed tax if the corporate veil is pierced; they may also be charged with money laundering or tax evasion if the shell structure is used to hide the true principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Adjustment and Deficient Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fraudulent intra-group pricing: excessively high management fees paid to a parent company, abusive royalty payments for notional AI IP, or sales to a related foreign distributor at below-market prices. Failure to maintain TP Documentation File.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of profits to arm's length plus 40% penalty for missing or materially inaccurate documentation (increased to 80% in cases of bad faith or fraud). Interest at 0.2% per month applies. Directors can be civilly liable if they knowingly signed misleading returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for TP adjustments, but if they intentionally set non-arm's length conditions for personal benefit or to evade tax, they can be personally liable and prosecuted for tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion (Dividend Stripping / Non-payment of WHT)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits to a non-resident shareholder without applying the statutory 25% or 30% withholding, or using artificial loans, royalties, or service fees to strip profits without withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid withholding tax plus late interest; 80% penalty for concealed distributions. Criminal prosecution under Article 1743 for non-payment of tax withheld at source: imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to €75,000. As a withholding agent, the SARL is primarily liable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative (gérant) is personally liable for the withheld tax if they knowingly failed to remit it; criminal liability and travel bans apply. Civil liability to the tax authority for the full unpaid amount.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML & Sanctions Violations (Money Laundering, Search of Terrorist Financing)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The stock photo platform accepts payments from sanctioned jurisdictions (e.g. Russia, Belarus) via Stripe/PayPal, fails KYC/AML screening of high-volume AI vendors, or processes payments for fraudulent image licensing or terrorism-linked receipts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the French Monetary and Financial Code (Articles L.561-1 et seq.) up to €1,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for entities subject to AML obligations. Criminal money laundering penalties: imprisonment up to 5 years (7 years for aggravating circumstances) and fines up to €375,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be criminally prosecuted for money laundering if they knowingly processed proceeds from illicit activities. Travel bans, asset freezes, and seizure of company assets. Beneficial owners are subject to investigation and may face extradition or direct financial liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Incorrect Use of Tax Credit or Reduced VAT Regime
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming the CIR for non-qualifying AI activities, applying the reduced VAT rate to standard stock photo licensing, artificially splitting turnover to remain under the €10 million reduced-rate threshold, or failing to collect VAT on digital sales to French customers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of the undue tax credit or VAT with interest, 40% penalty for inaccurate returns, and 80% for deliberate fraud. Criminal sanctions in severe cases. Directors may be personally liable if they signed incorrect declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are responsible for the completeness and accuracy of tax returns; personal liability arises where gross negligence or wilful misrepresentation is proven, triggering joint and several recovery and, in extreme cases, criminal penalties.
